 Mike Lupica: Time for the Jets to press reset on their reset

 EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY – SEPTEMBER 20: Breece Hall #20 of the New York Jets runs against the Green Bay Packers during their game at MetLife Stadium on September 20, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) 
 By Mike Lupica | New York Daily News PUBLISHED: November 7, 2026 at 9:33 AM EST As another trade deadline in the National Football League is dead ahead – dead being the operative word for this Jets season – the question for the Jets and for their fans is this:
Are they about to do a reset on their reset?
 A year ago at the deadline, Darren Mougey traded away Sauce Gardner and Quinnen Williams, who were supposed to be a part of the Jets future until the Jets once again didn’t have one of those. Now you wonder if Breece Hall might be the next present and future star of theirs on his way out the door, maybe even to the other end of, well, the hall at Metlife Stadium, just because he would be every bit as good a fit for the Giants as Jonathan Taylor, and might come more cheaply than Taylor.
 The Jets are about to continue the longest streak in American major sports without a playoff appearance. They are about to have almost as many losing seasons in a row as the Los Angeles Angels. The owner of the team is now 8-30 since he fired Robert Saleh five games into the 2024 season.
 At the time, Woody Johnson said that replacing Saleh with defensive coordinator Jeff Ulbrich would bring a “spark of positivity.” We all see how that has worked out. Woody lit a spark all right, but burned down the house all over again in the process. You have to be good at something.
 Now the Jets are 2-6, and looking at 2-8 as their next two opponents are the Chiefs and Bills, both of whom appear to be playing in a different league than the Jets are, which is the way things have been since the team went to that second straight AFC Championship game when Mike Tannenbaum and Rex Ryan were in charge of Woody’s football operation. Jim Harbaugh’s Chargers haven’t even won a game this season and even their prospects aren’t as bleak as the Jets because they’ve got a talented young quarterback in Justin Herbert, as bad as Herbert has looked in an offense that seems to have been conceived in a bar.
 There will still be eight games left for Aaron Glenn’s team after the game on Sunday in Kansas City. Maybe Glenn’s team walks through the fire and upsets the Chiefs and does the same against the Bills next Sunday at MetLife. But who thinks that’s going to happen after what we’ve seen the last two Sundays when the Jets had eminently winnable games against the Dolphins and the Raiders? It was Damon Runyon who once wrote that the race isn’t always to the swift, nor the battle to the wrong, but that’s the way to bet. Who’s betting on the Jets right now?
 Their beaten-down fans, who keep hearing their own stadium sound like somebody else’s, are already looking forward to the next NFL draft, when the Jets will have two Top 5 picks and – most likely – a new coach, Sean McDermott or somebody else, because I don’t think Mike Tomlin would come here even if Mike was the one who lost a bet.
 No one around here thought that Woody had made a bad hire with Glenn, and thus made another mistake in a long line of them since Tannenbaum and Ryan had the Jets one win away from their first Super Bowl since Namath. Glenn was one of the hot coordinators, he was going to New Orleans if he didn’t come home to Jersey. He was a proud old Jet, and it seemed to make a lot of sense to keep things in the family.
 It hasn’t worked out. This season is now like all the others under Todd Bowles and Adam Gase and Saleh and, if only briefly, Ulbrich. The Jets aren’t just as bad an operation as there is in professional football; they are one of the worst in professional sports. You know the other teams to have the kind of playoff drought lately the Jets are having? The Sacramento Kings and the Buffalo Sabres.
 The reality for Woody’s Jets is that they have turned into what Dolan’s Knicks were before Leon Rose and Tom Thibodeau arrived at the Garden. So Woody is the kind of bad owner that Dolan was for over two decades before the 2025-26 Knicks happened in such a big and Jimmy ended up in his creamsicle sports jacket. That moment for the Knicks, by the way, is the only thing giving Jets fans hope right now. Because if Dolan could finally figure things out, anybody can.
 Even though the way things are going THAT’S not the way to bet.
 Whatever happens with Glenn and whatever happens the rest of the way, the Jets are about to start all over again with a rookie quarterback next season, the way they started over with Sam Darnold and then started over with Zach Wilson and then, just as a change of pace, they started over with old Gramps, Aaron Rodgers. It means they are about to do a reset at quarterback the way they have had one reset after another since they put that fright into the Steelers at old Heinz Field in the fourth quarter of the AFC Championship game of January, 2011.
 Here is what a lifelong Jets fan, and friend of mine, said on Friday:
 “To me, McDermott is the guy who makes a lot of sense, if he’d be willing to listen. Me? I think Woody needs to have his Leon Hess Moment, even if there isn’t a Parcells out there the way there was 30 years ago. He needs someone who can walk into the building and fall back on a track record of success. McDermott sure had one in Buffalo. Also worth noting that only one New York football coach has had any sustained success this century—Tom Coughlin, hired with a great track record at Boston College and Jacksonville.
 “Three first-round picks next spring, two very likely to be in Top 5. Considerable room to spend. Some playmakers on offense. There is reason to think there is light at the end of the tunnel. But it’s so dark right now you can’t be blamed to believe otherwise. Besides, we’ve heard this song before.”
 I wanted Glenn to make it, you’ve read that from me plenty of times. Jets fans badly wanted him to be the one to turn things around, or at least get them going in the right direction even without a star quarterback in the house. But he has won only five out of 25 games as the HC of the NYJ.
 It is the second Sunday in November. And barring a different kind of Miracle in the Meadowlands, another Jets season is already over. Now another trade deadline approaches. Maybe there won’t be another big selloff, maybe there will. Either way, when the season is over the Jets will be starting all over again all over again. My friend is right. The Jets are playing their song.
 Trap games, Jalen’s star turn, and Steinbrenner’s budget
 Put it this way on Giants vs. Eagles:
 Let’s not have a trap game turn into a trap door.
 It is quite fitting that a LIV tour started with Saudi blood money ends up drowning in red ink.
 There’s a lot of mascots over there at Fox News who need a hug right now.
 That means Sean and Jesse and Laura, those poor things.
 And don’t forget Greg, another one for whom this election cycle turned out to be a brain buster.
 If you love tennis, and it’s sort of on record that I sure do, the best news in the sport is that Carlos Alcaraz is healthy again.
 And looks as if he’s starting 2027 already.
 Jannik Sinner is a great player, and might win 10 majors before he’s through.
 Alcaraz is a genius.
 Can’t say it enough:
 “The Rainmaker” on USA is really, really good.
 Jalen Brunson was really good in “Law & Order: Special Victims Unit” the other night.
Not gonna lie:
 More than a little worried about Nicholas Cage as John Madden.
 You know who I root really hard for in the place the great Dan Jenkins called Saturday’s America?
 Arch Manning.
 And put me down as somebody who still thinks the kid is going to be a great pro someday.
 Speaking of college football, how does it work there?
 Every time a coach gets a $50 million buyout, another angel gets its wings?
 By the way? It was as inevitable as the tide that somebody was going to look for a luxury tax in that sport, and apparently that’s exactly what the SEC is about to do.
 That game in Houston last Sunday really was one of the most fun Giants regular season games in a long time.
 It really is fascinating that Hal Steinbrenner is one of the owners leading the charge for a salary cap.
 After 17 years without a World Series for the Yankees, it’s fair to say that the people in charge are exactly like the teams they keep assembling:
 They’re good, nobody would suggest they’re not.
 Just not good enough.
 If you haven’t yet read Tom Verducci’s “The Death of the Launch Angle Revolution” at si.com, you ought to, and not just because it’s an example of a tremendous baseball writer at the top of his game.
 The money paragraph, for my money, is this one:
 “The Brewers proved what does work in today’s game: flatter swings, deeper contact points and bat angles that can shoot fastballs the other day – yes, even on the ground. Launch angle is now old school. The Brewers are new school.”
 Still haven’t gotten my Knicks championship ring.
